agency_full: National Aeronautics and Space Administration / Jet Propulsion Laboratory
payload: Planetary flyby spacecraft; three RTG modules totalling ~470 W at launch (decaying to ~250 W today)
credit: © NASA / JPL-Caltech — U.S. Government work, public domain. Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object — about 165 AU from the Sun and travelling at ~17 km/s relative to it. Saturn is the catalogued destination because Voyager 1's mission profile ended there; its Titan flyby (1980-11-12) bent the trajectory upward out of the ecliptic plane, and after that no further planetary encounter was possible. The spacecraft crossed the heliopause on 2012-08-25 — the first human-made object to enter interstellar space. Pale Blue Dot family photograph taken 1990-02-14 from a heliocentric distance of ~6 billion km. Mission planning credit: Gary Flandro, JPL, who identified the late-1970s outer-planet alignment that made the Grand Tour possible.
